                    "worker_error",
                    extra={"url": url, "worker_id": worker_id},
                )
            finally:
                self._frontier.task_done()

    async def _process_url(self, url: str, worker_id: int) -> None:
        robots = self._require_robots()

        if not await robots.allowed(url):
            self.logger.info(
                "robots_disallowed",
                extra={"url": url, "worker_id": worker_id},
            )
            return

        result = await self._fetch(url)

        record: dict[str, Any] = {
            "url": result.url,
            "status": result.status,
            "content_type": result.content_type,
            "fetched_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
            "error": result.error,
        }

        if result.body is not None:
            record["bytes"] = len(result.body)
        else:
            record["bytes"] = 0

        textual = self._is_textual(result.content_type)

        if textual and result.body is not None:
            text = self._decode_body(result.body, result.content_type)
            record["body"] = text
        else:
            text = None

        await self._writer.write(record)

        if (
            result.status is None
            or not 200 <= result.status < 300
            or result.body is None
            or text is None
            or not self._is_html(result.content_type)
            or self._stop_event.is_set()
        ):
            return

        parser = LinkParser()

        try:
            parser.feed(text)
            parser.close()
        except Exception:
            self.logger.warning(
                "html_parse_failed",
                extra={"url": result.url},
                exc_info=True,
            )
            return

        for href in parser.links:
            if self._stop_event.is_set():
                break

            try:
                candidate = canonicalize_url(href, result.url)
            except InvalidURL:
                continue

            if not self._in_scope(candidate):
                continue

            await self._enqueue(candidate)

    async def _enqueue(self, url: str) -> bool:
        if not self._accepting:
            return False

        if not self._in_scope(url):
            return False

        async with self._seen_lock:
            if url in self._seen:
                return False
            self._seen.add(url)

        if not self._accepting:
            return False

        await self._frontier.put(url)
        return True

    async def _fetch(self, initial_url: str) -> FetchResult:
        current_url = initial_url

        for redirect_number in range(self.config.max_redirects + 1):
            if not self._in_scope(current_url):
                return FetchResult(
                    url=current_url,
                    status=None,
                    content_type=None,
                    body=None,
                    error="redirect_outside_allowed_domain",
                )

            robots = self._require_robots()
            if not await robots.allowed(current_url):
                return FetchResult(
                    url=current_url,
                    status=None,
                    content_type=None,
                    body=None,
                    error="redirect_disallowed_by_robots",
                )

            response = await self._request_with_retries(current_url)

            if isinstance(response, FetchResult):
                return response

            status, headers, body = response
            content_type = headers.get("Content-Type")

            if status in {301, 302, 303, 307, 308}:
                location = headers.get("Location")

                if not location:
                    return FetchResult(
                        url=current_url,
                        status=status,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        body=body,
                        error="redirect_without_location",
                    )

                if redirect_number >= self.config.max_redirects:
                    return FetchResult(
                        url=current_url,
                        status=status,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        body=None,
                        error="too_many_redirects",
                    )

                try:
                    next_url = canonicalize_url(location, current_url)
                except InvalidURL:
                    return FetchResult(
                        url=current_url,
                        status=status,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        body=None,
                        error="invalid_redirect",
                    )

                if not self._in_scope(next_url):
                    return FetchResult(
                        url=current_url,
                        status=status,
                        content_type=content_type,
                        body=None,
                        error="redirect_outside_allowed_domain",
                    )

                current_url = next_url
                continue

            return FetchResult(
                url=current_url,
                status=status,
                content_type=content_type,
                body=body,
                error=None,
            )

        return FetchResult(
            url=current_url,
            status=None,
            content_type=None,
            body=None,
            error="too_many_redirects",
        )

    async def _request_with_retries(
        self,
        url: str,
    ) -> tuple[int, dict[str, str], bytes] | FetchResult:
        session = self._require_session()
        domain = hostname_for_url(url)
        attempts = self.config.retries + 1

        for attempt in range(attempts):
            if self._stop_event.is_set() and attempt > 0:
                return FetchResult(
                    url=url,
                    status=None,
                    content_type=None,
                    body=None,
                    error="shutdown",
                )

            try:
                await self._limiter.wait(domain)

                self.logger.info(
                    "request_started",
                    extra={
                        "url": url,
                        "attempt": attempt + 1,
                    },
                )

                async with session.get(
                    url,
                    allow_redirects=False,
                ) as response:
                    body = await self._read_limited(response)

                    self.logger.info(
                        "request_finished",
                        extra={
                            "url": url,
                            "status": response.status,
                            "attempt": attempt + 1,
                        },
                    )

                    if (
                        response.status in self._RETRY_STATUSES
                        and attempt + 1 < attempts
                    ):
                        await self._backoff(attempt)
                        continue

                    return (
                        response.status,
                        dict(response.headers),
                        body,
                    )

            except ResponseTooLarge:
                self.logger.warning(
                    "response_too_large",
                    extra={"url": url},
                )
                return FetchResult(
                    url=url,
                    status=None,
                    content_type=None,
                    body=None,
                    error="response_too_large",
                )
            except (aiohttp.ClientError, TimeoutError) as exc:
                self.logger.warning(
                    "request_failed",
                    extra={
                        "url": url,
                        "attempt": attempt + 1,
                        "error": type(exc).__name__,
                    },
                )

                if attempt + 1 >= attempts:
                    return FetchResult(
                        url=url,
                        status=None,
                        content_type=None,
                        body=None,
                        error=f"request_failed:{type(exc).__name__}",
                    )

                await self._backoff(attempt)

        return FetchResult(
            url=url,
            status=None,
            content_type=None,
            body=None,
            error="request_failed",
        )

    async def _read_limited(
        self,
        response: aiohttp.ClientResponse,
    ) -> bytes:
        content_length = response.content_length

        if (
            content_length is not None
            and content_length > self.config.max_response_bytes
        ):
            raise ResponseTooLarge

        result = bytearray()

        async for chunk in response.content.iter_chunked(64 * 1024):
            result.extend(chunk)

            if len(result) > self.config.max_response_bytes:
                raise ResponseTooLarge

        return bytes(result)

    async def _backoff(self, attempt: int) -> None:
        base = min(
            self.config.backoff_max,
            self.config.backoff_base * (2**attempt),
        )

        delay = random.uniform(0.0, base)

        try:
            await asyncio.wait_for(
                self._stop_event.wait(),
                timeout=delay,
            )
        except TimeoutError:
            pass

    def _in_scope(self, url: str) -> bool:
        try:
            return hostname_for_url(url) == self.allowed_hostname
        except InvalidURL:
            return False

    @staticmethod
    def _is_html(content_type: str | None) -> bool:
        if content_type is None:
            return False

        media_type = content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()
        return media_type in {"text/html", "application/xhtml+xml"}

    @staticmethod
    def _is_textual(content_type: str | None) -> bool:
        if content_type is None:
            return False

        media_type = content_type.split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()

        return (
            media_type.startswith("text/")
            or media_type == "application/xhtml+xml"
            or media_type == "application/json"
            or media_type.endswith("+json")
            or media_type.endswith("+xml")
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _decode_body(body: bytes, content_type: str | None) -> str:
        charset = "utf-8"

        if content_type:
            for parameter in content_type.split(";")[1:]:
                name, separator, value = parameter.strip().partition("=")
                if separator and name.lower() == "charset":
                    charset = value.strip("\"' ")
                    break

        try:
            return body.decode(charset, errors="replace")
        except LookupError:
            return body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

    def _require_session(self) -> aiohttp.ClientSession:
        if self._session is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Crawler session has not been initialized")
        return self._session

    def _require_robots(self) -> RobotsManager:
        if self._robots is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Robots manager has not been initialized")
        return self._robots


class ResponseTooLarge(Exception):
    pass

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import logging
from pathlib import Path

from webcrawler.canonical import InvalidURL
from webcrawler.crawler import Crawler, CrawlerConfig
from webcrawler.logging import configure_logging


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="webcrawler",
        description="Asynchronous, robots-aware, same-domain web crawler.",
    )

    parser.add_argument("url", help="Starting HTTP or HTTPS URL")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-o",
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=Path("crawl.jsonl"),
        help="Output JSONL file",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--concurrency",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Maximum number of crawler workers",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--rate",
        type=float,
        default=2.0,
        help="Maximum request starts per second per domain",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--retries",
        type=int,
        default=3,
        help="Number of retries after the initial request",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--backoff-base",
        type=float,
        default=0.5,
        help="Initial exponential retry backoff in seconds",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--backoff-max",
        type=float,
        default=30.0,
        help="Maximum exponential retry backoff in seconds",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--timeout",
        type=float,
        default=20.0,
        help="Total request timeout in seconds",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-redirects",
        type=int,
        default=10,
        help="Maximum redirects per URL",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--max-response-bytes",
        type=int,
        default=5_000_000,
        help="Maximum response body size",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--frontier-size",
        type=int,
        default=10_000,
        help="Maximum queued URLs",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--user-agent",
        default="ProductionCrawler/1.0",
        help="HTTP and robots.txt user agent",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--log-level",
        choices=["DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"],
        default="INFO",
        help="Logging level",
    )

    return parser


async def async_main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    config = CrawlerConfig(
        start_url=args.url,
        output=args.output,
        concurrency=args.concurrency,
        requests_per_second=args.rate,
        retries=args.retries,
        backoff_base=args.backoff_base,
        backoff_max=args.backoff_max,
        request_timeout=args.timeout,
        max_redirects=args.max_redirects,
        max_response_bytes=args.max_response_bytes,
        user_agent=args.user_agent,
        frontier_size=args.frontier_size,
    )

    crawler = Crawler(config)
    crawler.install_signal_handlers()
    await crawler.run()


def main() -> None:
    parser = build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args()

    configure_logging(args.log_level)

    try:
        asyncio.run(async_main(args))
    except (ValueError, InvalidURL) as exc:
        logging.getLogger("webcrawler").error(
            "configuration_error",
            extra={"error": str(exc)},
        )
        raise SystemExit(2) from exc
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logging.getLogger("webcrawler").info("interrupted")

import pytest

from webcrawler.canonical import InvalidURL, canonicalize_url, hostname_for_url


def test_removes_fragment() -> None:
    assert canonicalize_url("https://Example.COM/a#section") == "https://example.com/a"


def test_resolves_relative_url() -> None:
    assert (
        canonicalize_url("../next", "https://example.com/a/b/page.html")
        == "https://example.com/a/next"
    )


def test_normalizes_dot_segments() -> None:
    assert (
        canonicalize_url("https://example.com/a/./b/../c")
        == "https://example.com/a/c"
    )


def test_normalizes_default_ports() -> None:
    assert canonicalize_url("http://example.com:80/a") == "http://example.com/a"
    assert canonicalize_url("https://example.com:443/a") == "https://example.com/a"


def test_preserves_non_default_port() -> None:
    assert (
        canonicalize_url("http://example.com:8080/a")
        == "http://example.com:8080/a"
    )


def test_normalizes_unreserved_percent_encoding() -> None:
    assert (
        canonicalize_url("https://example.com/%7Euser?q=%41%2f")
        == "https://example.com/~user?q=A%2F"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        "mailto:test@example.com",
        "javascript:alert(1)",
        "ftp://example.com/file",
        "file:///tmp/file",
    ],
)
def test_rejects_non_http_schemes(url: str) -> None:

        canonicalize_url(url)


def test_rejects_credentials() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(InvalidURL):
        canonicalize_url("https://user:password@example.com/")


def test_hostname_is_case_insensitive() -> None:

    times: list[float] = []

        await limiter.wait("example.com")
        times.append(time.monotonic())

    await asyncio.gather(
        limiter.wait("a.example"),
        limiter.wait("b.example"),
    )

    elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
    assert elapsed < 0.5

Concurrency is bounded in two places. There are exactly `--concurrency` crawler workers, and the aiohttp connector independently caps simultaneous connections. The per-domain limiter serializes request-start reservations for a hostname and spaces them by `1/rate` seconds. Retries pass through the same limiter, so retries cannot bypass rate limits. Exponential backoff uses full jitter between zero and the capped exponential delay.

URLs are canonicalized before entering the frontier, and the canonical URL is inserted into `_seen` atomically before queueing. Fragments are removed, hostnames/default ports/percent escapes/dot segments are normalized, relative links are resolved against the fetched URL, and unsupported schemes are rejected. Scope is an exact IDNA-normalized hostname comparison, so `sub.example.com` is not treated as equivalent to `example.com`. Redirects are deliberately handled manually; aiohttp is never allowed to automatically follow one before the crawler verifies its destination and robots rules.

SIGINT/SIGTERM switch the crawler into shutdown mode. No new URLs are accepted, workers already holding requests finish their current operation, queued work is consumed without new network requests, `Queue.join()` therefore reaches zero, workers are cancelled only after the frontier is settled, the aiohttp session closes, and finally the JSONL writer is closed after its already-enqueued records have been written. Results are sent to the writer as pages finish rather than accumulated into a page collection, so crawler memory usage does not grow with the total number of downloaded page bodies. The duplicate URL set does necessarily grow with the number of discovered canonical URLs; exact duplicate suppression inherently requires retaining that state unless it is moved to an external/disk-backed store.

The concurrency design I would use is nevertheless important to pin down before generating the repository:

- `Board` has a monotonically increasing `version`.
- `Card` has its own monotonically increasing `version`.

- A move executes in a PostgreSQL transaction and obtains a row lock on the board (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`). It then verifies both versions while holding that lock.
- If either expected version is stale, the transaction makes no changes and returns a `CONFLICT` response containing the current authoritative board snapshot/version.
- Otherwise it calculates the complete affected ordering, updates positions safely inside the transaction, increments the moved card's version and board version, and commits.
- Only after commit does the server broadcast the resulting authoritative operation/snapshot to subscribed WebSocket clients.
- Consequently, two clients attempting to move the same card from version N cannot both succeed. The first transaction commits version N+1; the second waits for the board lock and then fails its version check. There is no last-writer-wins corruption.

- HTTP authentication uses an opaque, random session ID in an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie. Only a hash of that token is stored in PostgreSQL. Login rotates the session.
- State-changing HTTP requests use a synchronizer CSRF token associated with the session and supplied in a request header. WebSocket upgrades additionally validate `Origin`, the authenticated session cookie, and a CSRF token passed in the initial authenticated protocol message.
- All board reads/mutations and WebSocket subscriptions independently check board membership server-side; client state is never treated as authorization.

# Design Documentation: `useDebouncedSearch`

## 1. What it does

`useDebouncedSearch` gives a component two versions of the same text: `query`, which updates instantly on every keystroke for responsive UI rendering, and `debounced`, which only updates after the user has paused typing for `delay` milliseconds. It exists to let expensive operations (API calls, filtering large lists) wait for the user to "settle" before firing, without blocking the input field itself from feeling instant.

## 2. Why this design, not the alternatives

The core architectural bet here is: **use the browser's native timer primitives directly inside `useEffect`, with an explicit cleanup, rather than reaching for a library or a different rate-limiting strategy.** That bet is worth defending against three real alternatives.

| Approach | Pros | Cons | When to prefer it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`setTimeout` + `clearTimeout` in `useEffect`** (this implementation) | Zero dependencies; behavior is fully visible and auditable in ~5 lines; cleanup is idiomatic React (effect teardown maps 1:1 to timer teardown); `delay` can change at runtime because it's a dependency | You're re-implementing debounce logic yourself — easy to get subtly wrong (e.g. forgetting the dependency array or the cleanup) | Small/medium codebases, or any codebase trying to avoid a lodash dependency just for one function; teams that want the mechanism to be inspectable by any React dev without reading library internals |
| **`lodash.debounce` called inside `useEffect`, no cleanup, or debounce created fresh on every render** | Battle-tested debounce implementation; supports leading/trailing edge options out of the box | If you don't memoize it with `useMemo`/`useCallback` and don't cancel it on unmount, you get a *new* debounced function every render — the debounce window resets constantly and never actually accumulates delay. Without cleanup, a pending call can fire after the component unmounts, calling `setState` on an unmounted component | Only when you also correctly memoize the debounced function AND wire its `.cancel()` into the effect's cleanup — at which point it's roughly equivalent to this implementation but with more surface area to misuse |
| **Throttling instead of debouncing** (e.g. `lodash.throttle`, or a manual "fire at most once per N ms") | Guarantees regular, predictable update cadence — useful for things like scroll position or continuous drag events where you want *some* signal even while the input is still changing | Wrong tool for search: it fires while the user is still typing, so you'd send half-typed queries (e.g. "rea" then "reac" then "react") instead of waiting for them to stop | Continuous, ongoing input streams (scroll, resize, mousemove) where you want periodic sampling — not for "wait until the user is done" scenarios like search-as-you-type |

The one-sentence version: debounce vs throttle is a decision about *what you're waiting for* (silence vs. a fixed cadence), and native timers vs. a library is a decision about *who owns the cleanup contract* — here, React's effect lifecycle owns it directly, which is the safest place for it to live.

(Minor, non-architectural choices — the `delay = 300` default, returning a tuple instead of an object, using two `useState` calls instead of one `useReducer` — are ergonomic/stylistic and don't materially change behavior, so they aren't compared above.)

## 3. Failure modes if you removed the cleanup function

Remove `return () => clearTimeout(timer);` and the effect becomes: schedule a timer, never cancel the previous one. Here's what actually happens, keystroke by keystroke, typing "cat" with a 300ms delay:

1. **t=0ms** — User types `c`. `query` becomes `"c"`. Effect runs, schedules **Timer A**: "set debounced to `'c'` at t=300ms."
2. **t=100ms** — User types `a`. `query` becomes `"ca"`. Effect runs again (because `query` changed), schedules **Timer B**: "set debounced to `'ca'` at t=400ms." Without cleanup, **Timer A is still alive** — it was never cancelled.
3. **t=200ms** — User types `t`. `query` becomes `"cat"`. Effect runs again, schedules **Timer C**: "set debounced to `'cat'` at t=500ms." Timers A and B are both still pending.
4. **t=300ms** — **Timer A fires.** `debounced` is set to `"c"` — a stale, single-character value — even though the user has already typed the full word and moved on. Any effect watching `debounced` (e.g. "fire search API call") now fires a request for `"c"`.
5. **t=400ms** — **Timer B fires.** `debounced` is set to `"ca"`. Another stale API call, for a query the user never intended to search.
6. **t=500ms** — **Timer C fires.** `debounced` is finally set to `"cat"`, the correct value.

Net effect: instead of one debounced update ("cat" at t=500ms), you get three — "c", "ca", "cat" — each firing whatever expensive side effect `debounced` was meant to gate. This defeats the entire purpose of debouncing: you're now making a request per keystroke anyway, just delayed and out of sync with what's on screen. The bug is also silent — nothing throws an error, no console warning — which makes it a classic "works in the demo, chokes under real typing speed" defect.

A second, separate failure mode: if the component unmounts while a timer is pending (e.g. user navigates away mid-search), the orphaned timer still fires and calls `setState` on an unmounted component, which React will warn about (or silently no-op, depending on version) and which represents a memory/reference leak in the meantime.

## 4. How to explain this to someone who has never seen debouncing

Imagine you're a barista, and every time a customer says a word, you immediately run to the espresso machine and start making a drink based on what you've heard so far. Customer says "I'd like a—", you start making an "I'd" drink. They say "large", you scrap it and start an "I'd like a large" drink. By the time they finish their full order ("a large iced latte"), you've already wasted five drinks on partial orders.

A smarter barista waits until the customer *stops talking* for a beat — a brief pause that signals "I'm done" — before starting to make anything. If the customer starts talking again before that pause is over, the barista resets the wait and listens some more.

That pause-and-reset behavior is debouncing. `query` is "everything the customer has said so far" — you show it back to them instantly so they know you're listening (the text in the input box updates immediately). `debounced` is "what the barista actually acts on" — it only updates once the customer has been quiet for `delay` milliseconds, so you don't waste effort (API calls, filtering, computation) on a request that isn't finished yet.

## 5. Understanding checklist

Before an AI (or developer) claims to understand this pattern, it should be able to answer "yes" to all of the following:

- [ ] Can explain *why there are two separate state variables* (`query` for immediate UI feedback, `debounced` for gated side effects) rather than just one.
- [ ] Can explain what would go wrong, with a concrete keystroke-by-keystroke example, if the cleanup function were removed.
- [ ] Can articulate the difference between debounce and throttle *in terms of what problem each solves*, not just "one is different from the other."
- [ ] Can explain why `delay` must appear in the effect's dependency array (so that changing the delay at runtime doesn't use a stale closure value).
- [ ] Can identify that the cleanup function runs *both* on every re-render before the next effect *and* on unmount — and explain why both cases matter here (canceling superseded timers vs. preventing post-unmount `setState`).
- [ ] Can describe, without looking at the code, what would visibly happen in the UI if you typed quickly vs. slowly with this hook wired to a search API.
- [ ] Can state why this problem is solved with React's effect lifecycle rather than a manually managed `useRef` timer with no cleanup at all.

    <script>
        // Initialize CSS Variables
        const root = document.documentElement;
        const spotlight = document.getElementById('spotlight');
        
        // State for velocity calculation
        let mouseX = window.innerWidth / 2;
        let mouseY = window.innerHeight / 2;
        let lastX = mouseX;
        let lastY = mouseY;
        let velocity = 0;
        let rafId = null;
        let isMoving = false;
        let moveTimeout = null;

        // Throttled mouse tracking with velocity calculation
        document.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {
            mouseX = e.clientX;
            mouseY = e.clientY;
            
            if (!isMoving) {
                isMoving = true;
                updateSpotlight();
            }
            
            // Calculate velocity
            const dx = mouseX - lastX;
            const dy = mouseY - lastY;
            velocity = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
            
            // Reset last position
            lastX = mouseX;
            lastY = mouseY;
            
            // Clear existing timeout
            clearTimeout(moveTimeout);
            moveTimeout = setTimeout(() => {
                isMoving = false;
                // Gradually reduce spotlight size when mouse stops
                reduceSpotlight();
            }, 100);
        });

        function updateSpotlight() {
            if (!isMoving) return;
            
            // Update CSS custom properties
            root.style.setProperty('--x', mouseX);
            root.style.setProperty('--y', mouseY);
            
            // Map velocity to spotlight size (faster = wider)
            // Base size: 300px, max additional: 200px based on velocity
            const baseSize = 300;
            const maxAdditional = 200;
            const targetSize = baseSize + Math.min(velocity * 2, maxAdditional);
            
            root.style.setProperty('--spotlight-size', `${targetSize}px`);
            
            rafId = requestAnimationFrame(updateSpotlight);
        }

        function reduceSpotlight() {
            const currentSize = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--spotlight-size'));
            const baseSize = 300;
            
            if (currentSize > baseSize) {
                root.style.setProperty('--spotlight-size', `${currentSize - 10}px`);
                requestAnimationFrame(reduceSpotlight);
            }
        }

        // Parallax Effect on Mouse Move
        document.addEventListener('mousemove', (e) => {
            const x = (e.clientX / window.innerWidth - 0.5) * 2;
            const y = (e.clientY / window.innerHeight - 0.5) * 2;
            
            root.style.setProperty('--parallax-x', x * 10);
            root.style.setProperty('--parallax-y', y * 10);
        });

        // Intersection Observer for Scroll-Triggered Lighting
        const observerOptions = {
            root: null,
            rootMargin: '0px',
            threshold: 0.3
        };

        const sectionObserver = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
            entries.forEach(entry => {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                    entry.target.classList.add('in-view');
                    
                    // Temporarily increase spotlight intensity when section enters
                    const originalSize = getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue('--spotlight-size');
                    root.style.setProperty('--spotlight-size', '500px');
                    setTimeout(() => {
                        root.style.setProperty('--spotlight-size', originalSize);
                    }, 600);
                } else {
                    entry.target.classList.remove('in-view');
                }
            });
        }, observerOptions);

        // Observe all section titles
        document.querySelectorAll('[data-animate]').forEach(el => {
            sectionObserver.observe(el);
        });

        // Theme Toggle
        const themeToggle = document.getElementById('themeToggle');
        const html = document.documentElement;
        
        // Check for saved theme preference
        const savedTheme = localStorage.getItem('theme') || 'dark';
        html.setAttribute('data-theme', savedTheme);
        
        themeToggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
            const currentTheme = html.getAttribute('data-theme');
            const newTheme = currentTheme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
            
            html.setAttribute('data-theme', newTheme);
            localStorage.setItem('theme', newTheme);
            
            // Add transition class for smooth color interpolation
            html.style.transition = 'all 0.5s ease';
            setTimeout(() => {
                html.style.transition = '';
            }, 500);
        });

        // Smooth scroll for navigation links
        document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]').forEach(anchor => {
            anchor.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
                e.preventDefault();
                const target = document.querySelector(this.getAttribute('href'));
                if (target) {
                    target.scrollIntoView({
                        behavior: 'smooth',
                        block: 'start'
                    });

        document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
            if (document.hidden) {
                document.body.style.animationPlayState = 'paused';
            } else {
                document.body.style.animationPlayState = 'running';
            }
        });

        // Initialize spotlight position to center
        root.style.setProperty('--x', window.innerWidth / 2);
        root.style.setProperty('--y', window.innerHeight / 2);

            bottom: 20px;
            width: 200px;
            height: 150px;
            background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6);
            border: 1px solid var(--border-subtle);
            border-radius: 8px;
            overflow: hidden;
            pointer-events: all;
        }

        #minimap-content {
            position: absolute;
            transform-origin: 0 0;
        }

        .minimap-node {
            position: absolute;
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3);
            border-radius: 2px;
        }

        .minimap-viewport {
            position: absolute;
            border: 2px solid rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.8);
            background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.1);
            cursor: move;
        }

        /* Command Palette */
        #command-palette {
            position: absolute;
            top: 50%;
            left: 50%;
            transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
            width: 600px;
            max-height: 400px;
            background: var(--glass-bg);
            backdrop-filter: blur(20px);
            border: 1px solid var(--glass-border);
            border-radius: 12px;
            box-shadow: 0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.8);
            display: none;
            flex-direction: column;
            pointer-events: all;
            z-index: 2000;
        }

        #command-palette.active {
            display: flex;
        }

        .palette-input {
            width: 100%;
            background: transparent;
            border: none;
            border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-subtle);
            color: var(--text-primary);
            padding: 20px;
            font-size: 16px;
            outline: none;
        }

        .palette-results {
            max-height: 300px;
            overflow-y: auto;
        }

        .palette-item {
            padding: 12px 20px;
            cursor: pointer;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 12px;
            transition: background 0.2s;
        }

        .palette-item:hover, .palette-item.selected {
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1);
        }

        .palette-icon {
            width: 24px;
            height: 24px;
            border-radius: 4px;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            font-size: 12px;
        }

        .palette-icon.input { background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.2); color: var(--input-color); }
        .palette-icon.process { background: rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.2); color: var(--process-color); }
        .palette-icon.output { background: rgba(236, 72, 153, 0.2); color: var(--output-color); }

        /* Radial Menu */
        #radial-menu {
            position: absolute;
            width: 200px;
            height: 200px;
            pointer-events: none;
            display: none;
            z-index: 1500;
        }

        #radial-menu.active {
            display: block;
        }

        .radial-item {
            position: absolute;
            width: 60px;
            height: 60px;
            background: var(--glass-bg);
            border: 1px solid var(--glass-border);
            border-radius: 50%;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            cursor: pointer;
            pointer-events: all;
            transition: transform 0.2s, background 0.2s;
            font-size: 20px;
        }

        .radial-item:hover {
            transform: scale(1.1);
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15);
        }

        /* Toast Notifications */
        #toast-container {
            position: absolute;
            bottom: 20px;
            left: 50%;
            transform: translateX(-50%);
            display: flex;
            flex-direction: column;
            gap: 8px;
            pointer-events: none;
        }

        .toast {
            background: var(--glass-bg);
            border: 1px solid var(--glass-border);
            padding: 12px 24px;
            border-radius: 8px;
            font-size: 13px;
            animation: slide-up 0.3s ease;
            backdrop-filter: blur(10px);
        }

        @keyframes slide-up {
            from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
            to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
        }

        /* Particle Effects */
        .particle {
            position: absolute;
            pointer-events: none;
            border-radius: 50%;
            animation: particle-fade 0.6s ease-out forwards;
        }

        @keyframes particle-fade {
            0% { transform: translate(0, 0) scale(1); opacity: 1; }
            100% { transform: translate(var(--tx), var(--ty)) scale(0); opacity: 0; }
        }

        /* Scrollbar */
        ::-webkit-scrollbar {
            width: 8px;
            height: 8px;
        }

        ::-webkit-scrollbar-track {
            background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2);
        }

        ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb {
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2);
            border-radius: 4px;
        }

        ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb:hover {
            background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3);
        }
    </style>
</head>
<body>

<div id="canvas-container">
    <div id="grid-background"></div>
    <div id="transform-layer">
        <svg id="svg-layer"></svg>
        <div id="nodes-container"></div>
        <div id="groups-container"></div>
    </div>
    <div id="selection-box"></div>
</div>

<div id="ui-layer">
    <div id="sidebar">
        <div class="sidebar-header">
            <div class="sidebar-title">NexusFlow</div>
            <div style="font-size: 11px; color: var(--text-secondary); margin-top: 4px;">v2.4.0 • Procedural Graph</div>
        </div>
        <div class="sidebar-content">
            <div class="property-group">
                <div class="property-label">Graph Settings</div>
                <input type="text" class="property-input" placeholder="Graph Name" value="Untitled Workflow">
            </div>
            <div class="property-group">
                <div class="property-label">Statistics</div>
                <div style="font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-secondary); line-height: 1.6;">
                    Nodes: <span id="stat-nodes">0</span><br>
                    Connections: <span id="stat-edges">0</span><br>
                    Groups: <span id="stat-groups">0</span>
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="property-group">
                <div class="property-label">Validation</div>

                    ✓ No circular dependencies
                </div>
            </div>

        <div class="toolbar">
            <button class="btn" onclick="graphManager.autoLayout()">Auto Layout</button>
            <button class="btn primary" onclick="graphManager.executeGraph()">Execute</button>

            <button class="btn" onclick="graphManager.exportGraph()">Export JSON</button>
            <button class="btn" onclick="document.getElementById('import-file').click()">Import</button>
            <input type="file" id="import-file" style="display: none;" accept=".json">

    <div id="minimap">
        <div id="minimap-content"></div>
